offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 18:59:34Z set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. payments-api still stores and sends amounts in cents (pmt_000245 has amount_cents=1396), but with this setting the provider reads that number as dollars. So every charge since the deploy is 100 times too large: $13.96 became $1,396.00. Our payments, and the ledger entries booked from the provider's webhooks, no longer match the payments table. That breaks payments_match_provider with 63 findings, from pmt_000245 onward. The other invariants pass: the ledger books the provider's (inflated) amounts, so it balances and matches the provider. Refunds also pass, but some were issued for our cent amount: rfd_000024 refunded only 1396 cents of a $1,396.00 charge. Still open: I did not check a payment from just before the deploy (for example pmt_000244) to confirm it was correct, and I did not check the provider attempt metrics.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider failed with 63 findings, starting at pmt_000245. In every case the provider's charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents, for example 1396 vs 139600. The other four invariants pass.
payments-api was redeployed at 18:59:34Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It is the only change since the stack started at 18:58:08Z.
The first mismatched payment, pmt_000245, succeeded at 18:59:35.759Z, one second after the deploy, with amount_cents=1396. It was later refunded only 1396 (rfd_000024).

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 18:59:34Z deploy, so CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT goes back to cents and new charges are correct. Then repair the damage separately: for each of the 63 affected payments, refund the excess (99x our amount, minus anything already refunded) at the provider, and book those refunds in the ledger.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container restarts, so payment and refund requests fail or retry briefly. The rollback stops new overcharges, but the 63 charges already made stay overcharged until someone repairs them. If the previous unit setting was something other than cents, the rollback restores that setting instead.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy payments-api with the current settings (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars). That would bring back the overcharging, so do it only if the rollback itself breaks payments-api, and stop payment traffic while you do.
